ambiguities.evidence: The paper explicitly instructs the reader to take the first value u whenever u>u_FMA, even if another condition also holds. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: sentence immediately following (3.3)).
ambiguities.impact: A translation that treats the cases as unordered or confuses u with bar_u can assign the wrong effective rounding precision. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3) and priority sentence).
ambiguities.issue: The three conditions printed in (3.3) are intentionally overlapping because the first uses u while the latter two use bar_u. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3)).

ambiguities.evidence: Only left-to-right and right-to-left blocked summation are described concretely. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: derivation before (3.2) and paragraph after (3.4)).
ambiguities.impact: The universal-order claim should preserve the paper's wording rather than infer a stronger operational semantics. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: paragraph following (3.4)).
ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'all orders of evaluation' is not formalized as a precise class of expression trees. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: final sentence after (3.4)).

ambiguities.evidence: Setting u<=u_FMA and bar_u=u_FMA makes the second branch of (3.3) give tilde_u_FMA=0, after which (3.4) loses both tilde-gamma terms. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equations (3.3) and (3.4)).
ambiguities.impact: It must be labeled as a specialization by substitution, not as an independently stated theorem. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equations (3.3) and (3.4)).
ambiguities.issue: The exact same-precision specialization is derived rather than separately displayed. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equations (3.3) and (3.4)).

contract_plain_english: For each block-FMA dot product, the paper rewrites every computed term as the exact scalar product times one perturbation from chained output roundings and one from internal arithmetic. Their exact gamma bounds yield (3.4), including the mixed product term; right-to-left blocked summation permits the internal index q+b-1, and equal internal/FMA precision with no coarser final rounding removes the chained-rounding factor entirely. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: displayed factorization, equation (3.4), and following paragraph).

source_evidence.anchor: equations (2.3)-(2.6) and the paragraph defining gamma notation
source_evidence.observation: The paper uses the standard relative-error model, defines gamma_k(v)=kv/(1-kv), assumes kv<1 for relevant k and precisions, and explains that accents and the FMA superscript identify the associated unit roundoff.

source_evidence.anchor: Algorithm 3.1 and the paragraph immediately following it
source_evidence.observation: Algorithm 3.1 partitions the inner dimension into q=n/b blocks, converts operands to u_low if necessary, chains block FMAs with output precision u_FMA, optionally rounds to output precision u, and assumes no underflow or overflow in the analysis.

A dot product is evaluated through block partial sums s_i. Each block expression is evaluated at internal precision bar_u and then rounded according to the effective unit roundoff tilde_u_FMA defined in (3.3), with the first branch taking priority.

source_evidence.anchor: displayed factorization immediately before equation (3.4), equation (3.4), and the paragraph following it
source_evidence.observation: The computed dot product is factored as a sum of x_i y_i times two perturbation factors, with |alpha_i| bounded by tilde_gamma_q^FMA and |beta_i| bounded by bar_gamma_n. Equation (3.4) gives the resulting absolute forward-error bound; the following paragraph gives a sharper right-to-left index and states that (3.4) remains valid for every evaluation order of (3.1).

statement.algorithm_linkage: The contract concerns one scalar entry of the matrix product computed by the chained block-FMA loop on line 6 of Algorithm 3.1. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: Algorithm 3.1; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.1)).
binders: Let n,b,q be positive integers with q=n/b, so the n scalar products are grouped into q consecutive blocks of length b. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: definition of s_n and equation (3.1)).
Let x=(x_1,...,x_n) be a row of A, y=(y_1,...,y_n) a column of B, and s_n=x^T y=sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: paragraph introducing x, y, and s_n).
Let s_hat_i denote the computed block partial sums obtained from s_0=0 by (3.1), and let s_hat_n be the final computed dot product. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equations (3.1) and (3.2)).

Let bar_u be the internal block-FMA evaluation unit roundoff, u_FMA the block-FMA output unit roundoff, u the final output unit roundoff, and tilde_u_FMA the effective post-evaluation rounding parameter from (3.3). (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: prose before (3.2) and equation (3.3)).
conclusions: The displayed expansion tracks the first block as (x_1y_1(1+bar_theta_b^(1))+...+x_by_b(1+bar_theta_2^(1))) times prod_{j=2}^q(1+bar_theta_b^(j)) prod_{j=1}^q(1+delta_j), and the final block as (x_{n-b+1}y_{n-b+1}(1+bar_theta_{b+1}^(q))+...+x_ny_n(1+bar_theta_2^(q)))(1+delta_q), with intermediate blocks represented by the intervening ellipsis. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: displayed factorization immediately before (3.4)).

Equivalently, there exist alpha_i and beta_i such that s_hat_n=sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i(1+alpha_i)(1+beta_i), with |alpha_i|<=tilde_gamma_q^FMA and |beta_i|<=bar_gamma_n for every i. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: final line of the displayed factorization before (3.4)).
|s_n-s_hat_n| <= (tilde_gamma_q^FMA + bar_gamma_n + tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n) |x|^T|y|. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)).

For right-to-left evaluation of (3.1), which the paper identifies with blocked summation, bar_gamma_n may be replaced throughout (3.4) by bar_gamma_{q+b-1}. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: paragraph immediately following (3.4)).
The paper states that the unreduced bound (3.4) is valid for every order of evaluation of (3.1). (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: final sentence after equation (3.4)).

As an algebraic same-precision specialization, if u<=u_FMA and bar_u=u_FMA=v, then tilde_u_FMA=0 and (3.4) reduces exactly to |s_n-s_hat_n|<=gamma_n(v)|x|^T|y|; one may take alpha_i=0. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3), compact factorization, and equation (3.4)).
constants_and_indexing: The block-rounding factor uses q=n/b, while the internal-arithmetic factor uses n. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: compact factorization and equation (3.4)).

The first block has a b rather than b+1 leading theta index because s_0=0; the final block starts with index b+1 and ends with index 2. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: sentence and displayed factorization preceding (3.4)).
Right-to-left blocked summation changes the internal index from n to q+b-1, not merely to q. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: paragraph following (3.4)).
definitions_and_conventions: gamma_k(v)=kv/(1-kv); bar_gamma_k=gamma_k(bar_u); and tilde_gamma_k^FMA=gamma_k(tilde_u_FMA). (PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: gamma definition and accent convention).

Absolute values of vectors and matrices are componentwise, so |x|^T|y|=sum_i |x_i||y_i|. (PDF p. 3, printed C126, anchor: componentwise absolute-value convention; PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)).
Because s_0=0, the theta index on the x_1y_1 term is b rather than b+1; later block-leading terms use b+1. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: sentence immediately before the displayed factorization).
error_notions: Equation (3.4) is an absolute forward-error bound for the scalar dot product, not a relative-error or backward-error statement. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)).
The alpha_i and beta_i bounds are scalar multiplicative perturbation bounds on each exact product x_i y_i. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: compact factorization before (3.4)).
exceptional_values: Underflow and overflow are excluded by the standing analysis assumption. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: paragraph following Algorithm 3.1).

NaNs, infinities, and other exceptional IEEE values are not addressed in the selected analysis. (PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: standard model (2.3)-(2.4); PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: no-underflow-or-overflow assumption).
higher_order_terms: The mixed product tilde_gamma_q^FMA bar_gamma_n is retained in (3.4); the displayed coefficient is not truncated to first order. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)).

The only stated modeling omission is one of two possible successive output roundings; no explicit remainder bound for that omission is supplied. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: double-rounding paragraph before (3.2)).
hypotheses: The recurrence is s_i=s_{i-1}+sum_{j=(i-1)b+1}^{ib} x_j y_j for i=1,...,q, with each displayed right-hand side analyzed from left to right. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.1) and following sentence).

Floating-point operations obey fl(a op b)=(a op b)(1+delta), |delta|<=v, and gamma denominators are positive for all relevant indices and precisions. (PDF p. 4, printed C127, anchor: equations (2.3), (2.4), and gamma definition).

Equation (3.3) is read with priority: tilde_u_FMA=u if u>u_FMA; otherwise tilde_u_FMA=0 if bar_u>=u_FMA; otherwise tilde_u_FMA=u_FMA if bar_u<u_FMA. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3) and its priority clarification).
The analysis excludes underflow and overflow. (PDF p. 5, printed C128, anchor: paragraph following Algorithm 3.1).
implicit_context: This is the per-entry dot-product analysis underlying Algorithm 3.1, not yet the bound for initially converting arbitrary A and B to u_low. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: opening of section 3.2 and final paragraph of the page).

The exact same-precision reduction is obtained by substituting the equal precisions into (3.3) and (3.4); it is not presented on C129 as a separately numbered theorem. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equations (3.3) and (3.4)).
norms: No vector or matrix norm occurs; |x|^T|y| is the ordinary dot product of componentwise absolute values. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)).
numerical_model: Each block expression is evaluated at bar_u; its result is rounded to u_FMA and, when u>u_FMA, to final precision u. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: prose between equations (3.1) and (3.2)).

The local model is s_hat_i=[s_hat_{i-1}(1+bar_theta_b^(i))+x_{(i-1)b+1}y_{(i-1)b+1}(1+bar_theta_{b+1}^(i))+...+x_{ib}y_{ib}(1+bar_theta_2^(i))](1+delta_i), with |bar_theta_j|<=bar_gamma_j and |delta_i|<=tilde_u_FMA. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.2) and following text).
When two output roundings would occur, the analysis retains only one and calls the effect on the final bound negligible. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: double-rounding paragraph before (3.2)).

undebatable_constraints: The compact factorization has two distinct perturbation families with bounds tilde_gamma_q^FMA and bar_gamma_n. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: compact factorization before (3.4)).
The coefficient in (3.4) contains both gamma terms and their product. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)).
The right-hand factor is |x|^T|y|, not |x^Ty| and not a norm. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.4)).
The sharper right-to-left internal index is q+b-1. (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: paragraph following (3.4)).
The same-precision reduction requires tilde_u_FMA=0 under the branch priority in (3.3). (PDF p. 6, printed C129, anchor: equation (3.3) and its clarification).
